reason: The wheels need support on loose ground, so combining the metal stock and mesh seems like a practical way to make a crossing surface.
expectation: I expect to make some kind of traction mat or support for the drift, though I don't know exactly how it will be used.

alternatives.reason: The winch and anchor could help move the rover, but the immediate goal is to support its wheels.

effect: The panels can bridge the loose patch and give the wheels grip, so I should put them across the drift.
reaction: It is satisfying that the crosspieces spread weight while the mesh provides traction.
reason: Placing the traction panels on the soft drift directly supports the wheels.
expectation: I expect the panels to form a supported path across the loose ground, though the rover may still need the winch.

alternatives.reason: The anchored winch may help move the rover, but the panels address the immediate need for wheel support.

effect: The panels now support the wheel tracks, and the next goal is to move the rover onto firm rock.
reaction: The broad panels reaching the rock lip make the crossing easy to picture.
reason: Anchoring the winch is the only available combination and should help pull the rover across.
expectation: I expect the winch to attach to the rock anchor, though moving the rover may take another step.

effect: The winch line is anchored and aligned with the panels, ready to steady the rover across.
reaction: The line and panels have complementary roles, which makes the crossing feel practical.
reason: Combining the recovery line with the crossing is the only offered gameplay action and appears to be the way to move the rover onto firm ground.
expectation: I expect the rover to cross the panels under the winch's guidance and reach the rock lip.

effect: The rover reached the firm rock with the cold case secured, completing the crossing and bringing the sheltered ice face within reach.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the panels and winch work together as expected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the traction panels was most worthwhile: the explanation connected broad crosspieces with spreading wheel load and mesh with grip.

leastWorthwhile.text: Anchoring the winch felt the least engaging as a decision because it was the only gameplay action offered at that point.

surprise.text: I hadn't anticipated that the panels would be long enough to bridge the entire loose patch and reach the rock lip.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each had a clear role in supporting or steadying the rover.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to collect the second core and learn what the ice and specimen reveal, and the crossing made the practical journey engaging.
